description: A two-panel composite of misorientation distribution functions (MDFs, EBSD-derived) for an Fe-8% Al low-density steel deformed at 1100 °C; both panels are the same plot type. Each panel plots Frequency (linear y-axis, labelled 0, 0.025, 0.05, 0.075, 0.1) against Misorientation angle (°) (x-axis labelled 0 to 65 in 5° steps). In both panels a red vertical line at ~15° separates a red-labelled "LAB" region (left) from a red-labelled "HAB" region (right). A jagged black curve is the measured distribution; a smooth blue curve is the MacKenzie random distribution (per caption, ref [13]). Panel (a), strain rate 5 s^-1, prints "LAB : 20%", "HAB : 80%", "Average angle : 33.1°"; its black curve shows a small peak near 5° reaching the 0.025 gridline, then scattered values to ~60°. Panel (b), 10 s^-1, prints "LAB : 22%", "HAB : 78%", "Average angle : 32.9°"; its black curve has a much sharper low-angle peak near 5°, between the 0.05 and 0.075 gridlines. The blue MacKenzie curve peaks near 45° in both panels. The figure demonstrates that at 1100 °C the vast majority of boundaries are high-angle (>78%), and that the higher strain rate strongly intensifies the low-angle (subgrain) population while the average angle stays ~33°.
measured_quantities: frequency (dimensionless, fraction of boundaries per bin)

observations.observation: Both panels plot Frequency (y-axis, tick labels 0, 0.025, 0.05, 0.075, 0.1) against Misorientation angle (°) (x-axis, tick labels 0 to 65 in 5° increments).
A red vertical line at approximately 15° divides each panel into a red-labelled 'LAB' (low-angle boundary) region on the left and a red-labelled 'HAB' (high-angle boundary) region on the right.
Each panel contains a smooth blue curve that rises from near zero at low angle and peaks near 45°; the caption identifies this blue curve as the MacKenzie distribution [13].
The black measured curve in panel (a) shows only a modest low-angle peak near 5° that reaches about the 0.025 gridline, followed by a scattered distribution out to about 60°.
The black measured curve in panel (b) has a much sharper and taller low-angle peak near 5°, rising between the 0.05 and 0.075 gridlines, i.e. far above the MacKenzie reference at that angle.
In both panels the LAB/HAB boundary is drawn at about 15° and the blue MacKenzie curve lies well above the measured black curve in the 20-40° range.
The caption labels panel (a) as strain rate ε̇ = 5 s^-1 and panel (b) as 10 s^-1 (printed in the caption as 'ε = 10 s−1'), at 1100 °C.
The caption states the figure shows misorientation distribution functions at 1100 °C and that the blue curve displays the MacKenzie distribution [13].

The two panels show nearly identical high-angle-boundary fractions (80% vs 78%) and average misorientation angles (33.1° vs 32.9°), so the main difference between them is the strength of the low-angle peak, not the LAB/HAB balance.
The paper abstract states the study used hot torsion tests on an Fe–8% Al alloy over 900–1100 °C and 0.1–10 s^-1, conditions spanning the two strain rates of this figure.

subfigures.description: Misorientation distribution function at 1100 °C and 5 s^-1. Frequency (0-0.1) vs misorientation angle (0-65°); red vertical line at ~15° separating LAB from HAB. Printed values: LAB : 20%, HAB : 80%, Average angle : 33.1°. Jagged black measured curve has a small peak near 5° touching the 0.025 gridline; smooth blue MacKenzie reference curve rises to a maximum near 45°.

Misorientation distribution function at 1100 °C and 10 s^-1. Same axes and red LAB/HAB divider at ~15°. Printed values: LAB : 22%, HAB : 78%, Average angle : 32.9°. The black measured curve shows a pronounced narrow peak near 5° rising between the 0.05 and 0.075 gridlines, with a broader shoulder near 45°; the blue MacKenzie curve again peaks near 45°.
